lessons.title: Factors and multiples
lessons.art_alt: Hoot the white owl and Sumi the fox arrange 12 red apples in 3 rows of 4 on a pink picnic blanket in the orchard

hook.text: Hoot the owl and Sumi the fox are setting out a picnic in Abacus Orchard. They have 12 red apples, and Sumi lines them up in 3 neat rows of 4 on the pink blanket. Hoot wonders: can 12 apples make other neat rows too, with none left over?
hook.say: Hoot the owl and Sumi the fox are setting out a picnic in Abacus Orchard. They have 12 red apples, and Sumi lines them up in 3 neat rows of 4 on the pink blanket. Hoot wonders: can 12 apples make other neat rows too, with none left over?

discover.text: Make 3 equal rows of apples, one ring for each row. Drag an apple into a ring, or tap a ring to add one. Use all 12!
discover.hint: Every row gets the same: 4 apples each. Count in 4s: 4, 8, 12.
discover.say: Make 3 equal rows of apples, one ring for each row. Drag an apple into a ring, or tap a ring to add one. Use all 12!

rule.text: 3 rows of 4 make 12, so 3 × 4 = 12. 3 and 4 are factors of 12: they fit into 12 exactly, with nothing left over. And 12 is a multiple of 3 and of 4: it is in their times tables. 12 apples also make 1 row of 12, 2 rows of 6, 4 rows of 3, 6 rows of 2 and 12 rows of 1. So the factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.
examples: 5 is not a factor of 12: 12 ÷ 5 = 2 r 2
rule.say: 3 rows of 4 make 12, so 3 times 4 equals 12. 3 and 4 are factors of 12: they fit into 12 exactly, with nothing left over. And 12 is a multiple of 3 and of 4: it is in their times tables. 12 apples also make 1 row of 12, 2 rows of 6, 4 rows of 3, 6 rows of 2 and 12 rows of 1. So the factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.
sayEx: factor pairs of 12: 1 times 12, 2 times 6, 3 times 4
5 is not a factor of 12: 12 divided by 5 equals 2 remainder 2

check.q: Which number is a factor of 12?

notes.5: 12 apples can't make equal rows of 5: two rows use 10 and 2 are left over. 6 works: 2 rows of 6.
notes.24: 24 is a multiple of 12 (2 × 12). A factor fits into 12 exactly, like 6: 2 × 6 = 12.

check.explain: 2 × 6 = 12, so 6 fits into 12 exactly: it is a factor.
check.say: Which number is a factor of 12?

check.q: Which list shows ALL the factors of 8?

notes.2, 4: Don't forget 1 and 8! Every number has 1 and itself as factors: 1 × 8 = 8.
notes.1, 2, 4, 6, 8: 6 is not a factor of 8: 8 ÷ 6 = 1 r 2. The factor pairs are 1 × 8 and 2 × 4.

check.explain: The factor pairs of 8 are 1 × 8 and 2 × 4, so the factors are 1, 2, 4 and 8.
check.say: Which list shows ALL the factors of 8?

check.q: Which number is a multiple of 4?

notes.14: Count in 4s: 4, 8, 12, 16. 14 is skipped, because 14 ÷ 4 = 3 r 2.
notes.2: 2 is a factor of 4, not a multiple. Multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 …

check.explain: 4 × 5 = 20, so 20 is in the 4 times table: a multiple of 4.
check.say: Which number is a multiple of 4?

reteach.text: Here's another way: the no-leftovers test! To check if a number is a factor of 12, share 12 by it. If nothing is left over, it is a factor. 12 ÷ 4 = 3, nothing left, so 4 is a factor. 12 ÷ 5 = 2 r 2, so 5 is not. Multiples go the other way: count in that number's steps, like 4, 8, 12, 16.

items.why: 12 ÷ 5 = 2 r 2. Two apples are left over, so 5 is not a factor.
12 ÷ 8 = 1 r 4. Four apples are left over, so 8 is not a factor.
12 ÷ 7 = 1 r 5. Five apples are left over, so 7 is not a factor.

discover.text: Can 12 apples make equal rows of this size, with none left over? Drag each card into a basket, or tap a card and then a basket.
discover.hint: Share 12 by the number. Nothing left over means it is a factor.
discover.say: Can 12 apples make equal rows of this size, with none left over? Drag each card into a basket, or tap a card and then a basket.

reteach.say: Here's another way: the no-leftovers test! To check if a number is a factor of 12, share 12 by it. If nothing is left over, it is a factor. 12 divided by 4 equals 3, nothing left, so 4 is a factor. 12 divided by 5 equals 2 remainder 2, so 5 is not. Multiples go the other way: count in that number's steps, like 4, 8, 12, 16.

options: No, because 21 is an odd number

notes.No, because 21 is an odd number: Odd numbers have factors too! 21 ÷ 7 = 3 with nothing left over, so 7 is a factor.
notes.No, because 7 is bigger than 3: Size doesn't stop it. 7 fits into 21 exactly three times: 3 × 7 = 21.

check2.explain: 21 ÷ 7 = 3 with nothing left over, so 7 is a factor of 21.

check2.q: Which number is a common multiple of 2 and 3?

notes.5: 5 is not in the 2 times table or the 3 times table.
notes.8: 8 is a multiple of 2, but not of 3: 3, 6, 9 skips 8.

check2.say: Which number is a common multiple of 2 and 3?

check2.q: Mog has 18 stickers. He wants equal rows with none left over. Which row size will NOT work?

notes.rows of 3: Rows of 3 work: 6 rows of 3 = 18, none left over.
notes.rows of 6: Rows of 6 work: 3 rows of 6 = 18, none left over.

check2.explain: 18 ÷ 4 = 4 r 2, so rows of 4 leave 2 stickers over. 4 is not a factor of 18.
check2.say: Mog has 18 stickers. He wants equal rows with none left over. Which row size will NOT work?

lessons.grown: 👪 MOE P4 Whole Numbers: factors and multiples; finding all the factors of a number (factor pairs, shown as arrays), multiples of a number, common factors and common multiples; checking a factor by dividing with no remainder.

lessons.title: A fraction of a set
lessons.art_alt: Crumb the lilac dragon in a chef hat holds a tray of cupcakes beside 4 plates with 3 pink cupcakes on each, while Puffbun the bunny, Mog the grey cat and Hoot the owl wait at the counter

hook.text: Crumb the baker dragon baked 12 pink cupcakes. Puffbun, Mog and Hoot are waiting at the counter! Crumb says $\frac{1}{4}$ of the cupcakes are for the party game, and $\frac{3}{4}$ are for snack time. But how many cupcakes is a quarter of 12?
hook.say: Crumb the baker dragon baked 12 pink cupcakes. Puffbun, Mog and Hoot are waiting at the counter! Crumb says one quarter of the cupcakes are for the party game, and three quarters are for snack time. But how many cupcakes is a quarter of 12?

discover.text: A quarter means 4 equal parts. Share the 12 cupcakes fairly onto 4 plates. Tap 🃏 Deal one each, or tap a plate.
discover.hint: Deal one cupcake to every plate each time, until all 12 are shared.
discover.say: A quarter means 4 equal parts. Share the 12 cupcakes fairly onto 4 plates. Tap 🃏 Deal one each, or tap a plate.

rule.text: To find a fraction of a set, cut the set into equal groups. The bottom number says how many equal groups. The top number says how many groups you take. $\frac{1}{4}$ of 12: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so one group is 3 cupcakes. $\frac{3}{4}$ of 12 is 3 groups: 3 × 3 = 9 cupcakes.
rule.say: To find a fraction of a set, cut the set into equal groups. The bottom number says how many equal groups. The top number says how many groups you take. one quarter of 12: 12 divided by 4 equals 3, so one group is 3 cupcakes. three quarters of 12 is 3 groups: 3 times 3 equals 9 cupcakes.
sayEx: one quarter of 12 equals 12 divided by 4 equals 3
three quarters of 12 equals 3 times 3 equals 9
two thirds of 15: 15 divided by 3 equals 5, 2 times 5 equals 10

notes.3: 3 is how many groups. Share 15 into 3 equal groups: each group has 5.

notes.4: 4 is only $\frac{1}{3}$ of 12. Two thirds is 2 groups of 4: 8.
notes.6: 6 is half of 12. Cut 12 into 3 groups of 4 and take 2 groups: 8.

check.explain: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 in each group, and 2 groups make 2 × 4 = 8.

check.q: Crumb baked 20 cupcakes. $\frac{1}{4}$ of them have sprinkles. How many have sprinkles?

notes.4: 4 is how many equal groups. Each group has 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cupcakes.
notes.15: 15 is the cupcakes WITHOUT sprinkles, $\frac{3}{4}$ of them. One quarter is 5.

check.say: Crumb baked 20 cupcakes. one quarter of them have sprinkles. How many have sprinkles?

reteach.text: Here's another way: draw a bar model! Draw one long bar for the whole set, and cut it into equal boxes. The bottom number tells you how many boxes. Share the total into the boxes, then colour as many boxes as the top number. For two thirds of 15: 3 boxes of 5, colour 2 boxes, and that's 10.

items.s: One third of 15: 15 ÷ 3 = ___ in each box.
items.why: 15 shared into 3 equal boxes gives 5 in each.

items.s: Three thirds of 15 is all 3 boxes: ___
items.why: 3 out of 3 boxes is the whole set: 15.

discover.text: Mog has 15 fish treats. Use the bar model to find thirds of 15. Drag the right number into each gap, or tap it.
discover.hint: Share 15 into 3 equal boxes first. Then count how many boxes you need.
discover.say: Mog has 15 fish treats. Use the bar model to find thirds of 15. Drag the right number into each gap, or tap it.

reteach.say: Here's another way: draw a bar model! Draw one long bar for the whole set, and cut it into equal boxes. The bottom number tells you how many boxes. Share the total into the boxes, then colour as many boxes as the top number. For two thirds of 15: 3 boxes of 5, colour 2 boxes, and that's 10.

notes.5: 5 is how many groups. Share 20 into 5 equal groups: 4 in each.

notes.2: 2 is $\frac{1}{4}$ of 8, just one group. Take 3 groups: 3 × 2 = 6.
notes.4: 4 is half of 8. Three quarters is 3 groups of 2: 6.

check2.explain: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 in each group, and 3 groups make 6.

check2.q: Puffbun has 18 carrots. She eats $\frac{1}{3}$ of them. How many carrots does she eat?

notes.3: 3 is how many equal groups. Each group has 18 ÷ 3 = 6 carrots.

check2.say: Puffbun has 18 carrots. She eats one third of them. How many carrots does she eat?

lessons.grown: 👪 MOE P4 Fractions: fraction of a set of objects (e.g. ¾ of 12): dividing the set into equal groups by the denominator and taking as many groups as the numerator; the bar model for a fraction of a quantity.

lessons.title: Rounding: the number-line hill
lessons.art_alt: Puffbun the white bunny stands on top of a grassy hill with a big red ball, with a little cottage at the foot of each side

hook.text: Puffbun the bunny is on top of a grassy hill with a big red ball. At the foot of one side is the 40 cottage, and at the foot of the other side is the 50 cottage. The very top of the hill is 45. If Puffbun lets go of a ball, which cottage will it roll to?
hook.say: Puffbun the bunny is on top of a grassy hill with a big red ball. At the foot of one side is the 40 cottage, and at the foot of the other side is the 50 cottage. The very top of the hill is 45. If Puffbun lets go of a ball, which cottage will it roll to?

items.why: 41 is right next to the 40 cottage, far before the top at 45. It rolls back to 40.
43 is before the hilltop at 45, so it rolls back down to 40.
44 is just before the top. It is still on the 40 side, so it rolls back to 40.
45 is the very top! The rule is: halfway always rolls on, up to 50.
47 is past the top at 45, so it rolls on to 50.
49 is right next to the 50 cottage. It rolls on to 50.

discover.text: Each card is a ball on the hill between 40 and 50. Where will it roll? Drag each card into a cottage, or tap a card and then a cottage.
discover.hint: Look at the ones digit. 1, 2, 3 or 4: roll back to 40. 5, 6, 7, 8 or 9: roll on to 50.
discover.say: Each card is a ball on the hill between 40 and 50. Where will it roll? Drag each card into a cottage, or tap a card and then a cottage.

rule.text: Rounding to the nearest 10 means finding the closest ten. Look at the ones digit. 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4: round down to the ten before. 5, 6, 7, 8 or 9: round up to the next ten. A number exactly halfway always rounds up. To round to the nearest 100, do the same with the tens digit.
rule.say: Rounding to the nearest 10 means finding the closest ten. Look at the ones digit. 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4: round down to the ten before. 5, 6, 7, 8 or 9: round up to the next ten. A number exactly halfway always rounds up. To round to the nearest 100, do the same with the tens digit.

notes.60: 67 is past the hilltop at 65, so it rolls on up to 70.
notes.80: 80 is too far away. 67 sits between 60 and 70, and it is closer to 70.

check.explain: The ones digit is 7, so round up: 67 → 70.

notes.400: 450 is exactly halfway between 400 and 500, and halfway always rounds up: 500.
notes.450: Rounding to the nearest 100 gives a whole hundred. 450 is halfway, so it rounds up to 500.

check.q: Which number rounds to 30 when you round to the nearest 10?

notes.35: 35 is halfway between 30 and 40, and halfway rounds up to 40.
notes.24: 24 has a ones digit of 4, so it rounds down to 20.

check.explain: 34 has a ones digit of 4, so it rounds down to 30.
check.say: Which number rounds to 30 when you round to the nearest 10?

reteach.text: Here's another way: the neighbour digit tells the story! Find the place you round to, then look at the digit just to its right. To round 349 to the nearest 100, the hundreds digit is 3 and its neighbour, the tens digit, is 4. 4 is small, so 349 rounds down to 300. 351 has a tens digit of 5, so it rounds up to 400.

items.s: 349 to the nearest 100: the tens digit is 4, so ___
items.why: 4 is less than 5, so round down to 300.

items.s: 351 to the nearest 100: the tens digit is 5, so ___
items.why: 5 means round up, so 351 rounds up to 400.

items.s: 780 to the nearest 100: the tens digit is 8, so ___
items.why: 8 is 5 or more, so round up to 800.

discover.text: Round each number to the nearest 100. Look at the tens digit! Drag the right number into each gap, or tap it.
discover.hint: Tens digit 0 to 4: round down. Tens digit 5 to 9: round up.
discover.say: Round each number to the nearest 100. Look at the tens digit! Drag the right number into each gap, or tap it.

reteach.say: Here's another way: the neighbour digit tells the story! Find the place you round to, then look at the digit just to its right. To round 349 to the nearest 100, the hundreds digit is 3 and its neighbour, the tens digit, is 4. 4 is small, so 349 rounds down to 300. 351 has a tens digit of 5, so it rounds up to 400.

notes.80: 85 is exactly halfway between 80 and 90, and halfway rounds up: 90.
notes.85: Rounding to the nearest 10 gives a whole ten. 85 is halfway, so it rounds up to 90.

check2.explain: The ones digit is 5, so round up: 85 → 90.

notes.700: The tens digit of 628 is 2, which is small, so it rounds down to 600.
notes.630: 630 is 628 to the nearest 10. To the nearest 100, look at the tens digit 2: 600.

check2.explain: The tens digit is 2, so round down: 628 → 600.

check2.q: The orchard library has 238 books. About how many books is that, to the nearest 10?

notes.230: The ones digit is 8, so 238 rounds up to the next ten: 240.
notes.200: 200 is 238 to the nearest 100. To the nearest 10, look at the ones digit 8: 240.

check2.explain: The ones digit is 8, so round up: 238 → 240.
check2.say: The orchard library has 238 books. About how many books is that, to the nearest 10?

lessons.grown: 👪 MOE P4 Whole Numbers: rounding numbers to the nearest 10, 100 or 1000 and using ≈ (is approximately equal to); a number exactly halfway rounds up. This lesson covers the nearest 10 and 100 with the number-line hill; the practice round goes on to 1000.
